commons:144186874.summary: The jewelled cover of Emperor Henry II's book of Gospel readings frames an older ivory of the Crucifixion within gold, gems, pearls and enamel roundels of the evangelists' symbols. In the ivory, angels hover above the cross between the sun and moon, mourners and soldiers stand below, the holy women come to the tomb, and the dead rise from their graves, with Ocean and Earth at the bottom. The Ottonian goldsmiths thus enshrined a Carolingian masterpiece, honouring the crucified Christ with the most precious materials of the age.
facts: Wikipedia notes that the ivory plaque was carved around 870, probably in the circle of the Carolingian court school associated with Metz, and was reused in the 11th-century cover.
The manuscript, made for Henry II, the last Ottonian emperor, is a masterpiece of the Reichenau 'Liuthar group' of illuminators; it is now Clm 4452 in the Bavarian State Library.
The cover's inscription names Henry II; the Commons description links its making to the founding of the diocese of Bamberg in 1007.
commons:144186874.notes: Dating of the frame varies: Wikipedia gives c. 1014, the Commons description c. 1007 (foundation of Bamberg). Wikipedia also says Christ and the twelve apostles appear along the frame; this could not be confirmed at thumbnail size.
